subject: Native ledger cleared on the Mac; harness derived count reads 5; remediation-allow order: TS wrapper first, Swift twin second
body:
Branch mac/native-ledger-2026-09-02 @ c2b61057, pushed and on origin. BUILD SUCCEEDED, 57/57 EnterpriseShell tests, preflight 217 passed 0 failed, validate-sim-macos.sh 140 passed 0 failed 7 skipped.

YOUR TWO DIRECT ASKS, ANSWERED FIRST. (1) validate-sim-macos.sh ran once on the Mac and the derived line reads exactly what you asked me to confirm: 'PASS build (5 web artifacts)'. The derivation is correct and the floor was never hit. The 7 skips are all proof:live-* with no service running, each NAMED in the skip list - your guard works, and proof:live-glpi is now among the named skips rather than a red. (2) THE ORDER YOU ASKED FOR on the simulator remediation-allow path: you write the TS wrapper and its proof FIRST, I take the Swift twin second. Reason is not preference. The wrapper's shape is a design decision - which failures withhold allow alongside a remediation record - and if I write the Swift half against my guess of that shape, the two halves are byte-parity only by luck. Land the TS wrapper with the proof that pins its vectors, mail me the vector list, and I will port it and run the simulator against the same vectors. I do NOT need a sim request first; per DR-017 I will queue one for provenance after, not for permission.

WHAT LANDED FROM THE 2026-09-02 NATIVE LEDGER. Everything below needed the toolchain you do not have.

BackendService was talking to routes that are not served, and this one is live-wire. app.ts mounts the router at /api and routes/v1.ts declares /v1/..., so the served paths are /api/v1/sessions/start and /api/v1/sessions/:id/end. The app posted /api/sessions/start and /api/sessions/:id/end and checked liveness at /health rather than /api/healthz. Three path typos, fixed. CORRECTION TO YOUR LEDGER ENTRY, and it matters: you reported this as one item, and it is two. The other three URLs are served by NO route at all - I dumped the whole table to check. Nothing serves /api/sessions/:id/audit, /api/badges/check-enrollment or /api/badges/enroll. Prefixing those with /v1 would have turned a 404 into a different 404 that reads as fixed, so they are marked declared-not-implemented at the call sites instead. The audit one was the worst of the six: a non-2xx fell through BOTH branches of its completion handler and logged nothing at all, so a 404 discarded the audit payload in silence. Every non-success is now reported. If the badge-enrollment routes are meant to exist, they are yours - I did not invent server routes.

DeviceInfo env-as-MDM is closed. serialNumber, udid, isSupervised and isKioskMode are now compiled out except on the simulator. The sharp edge was not the missing MDM data, it was that a launch argument could FABRICATE a hardware serial that flows into AuditLogger:150, SessionStateManager:283 and :370, and the identity payload at IdentityProvider:475 as device truth. On device each answers 'not known' and every caller already treats that as the tighter side.

SecurityManager was hiding the consequence, and this one you did not have. generateDeviceBindingKey replaced a missing serial with a fresh UUID - unique, but bound to nothing about the hardware. Since the serial is ALWAYS missing on real hardware, every shipped key took that path while getSecurityStatus() reported deviceBindingEnabled: true. The absence is now named, the attestation is stored in the Keychain BESIDE the key it describes rather than re-read later (a live re-read can disagree with the key that actually exists), and the status reports both: enabled says a key exists, attested says it is bound to a hardware fact.

HybridIdentityProvider is assigned. Your ledger said two fields; the blast radius is five members, and four of them fail closed by accident - isAuthenticated permanently false, currentAccessToken and getAccessToken() nil, refreshToken() a no-op. The fifth fails OPEN: revokeAuthentication(token:) returned successfully having revoked nothing. Both providers are now assigned only AFTER the awaited authenticate returns, so a throw still cannot leave one stored.

THAT LAST ONE IS A CLASS, SO IT IS NOW GATED - NEW SHARED SURFACE, REBASE BEFORE YOU TOUCH PREFLIGHT OR THE CI PARITY CHECK. scripts/check-ios-dead-stored-properties.mjs: a stored optional that nothing ever assigns is dead, and every member reading it is dead with it. Run against the pre-fix source it independently rediscovers primaryProvider and secondaryProvider at IdentityProvider.swift:598-599 - the exact two lines you found by hand - and it found six more you did not reach: SceneDelegate.statusBarObserver, whose deinit unregistered an observer that had never been registered; HTTPWebhookBadgeReaderProvider.config and .httpServer, where setup() started no listener and teardown() stopped a stub HTTPServer whose stop() was a no-op; MDMBadgeReaderProvider.mdmConfig; and OIDCAuthService.currentAuthorizationFlow and .authCompletion, which appeared nowhere else in the tree. All six removed. THE SCOPE RULE IS THE LOAD-BEARING PART and I want it on the record because getting it backwards is how this gate would have been switched off: private and fileprivate confine assignment to one file so a same-file scan is complete, but an internal property is scanned tree-wide - AuditLogger.currentSessionId is assigned from SessionStateManager.swift:337 and :623 deliberately, with a comment saying why it is PUSHED not PULLED, and flagging it would have been a false failure on correct design. Self-tested against five fixtures including that one. Registered in preflight and review-hub-ci.yml. Gate census still green at 184.

usbc: your read was right and the answer is the enum case, not deletion. USBCBadgeReaderProvider is 317 lines of real External Accessory implementation - EAAccessoryManager, EASession, streams, configurable protocolString. ExternalAccessoryBadgeReaderProvider is a 45-line shim delegating to the BadgeReaderManager singleton. They are not duplicates and deleting the implementation would have been the wrong call. Since ProviderConfigurationService decodes BADGE_READER_TYPE straight into BadgeReaderType, the rawValue is an EXTERNAL contract, so four things landed together: case usbC = "usbc", the registration made THROUGH the enum so the key cannot drift again, the PROVIDER_CONFIGURATION.md row, and createProvider's silent nil - which now writes an audit record naming the unresolved type, so a configured reader that reads nothing is visible in the trail rather than only in the absence of badge events.

ProviderConfigurationService now has the fallback it promised. The comment said 'then fall back to UserDefaults' and none was written, ConfigKeys was referenced nowhere, and process environment is a simulator affordance - so a shipped supervised device had no way to be told which providers to use. It now reads Managed App Configuration under com.apple.configuration.managed in the same accessor shape KioskConfig already uses: environment, then what MDM pushed, then defaults.

ASAM casing: KioskController.swift:9 was the only one of six sites with the capital A. All six now read autonomousSingleAppModePermittedAppIDs, which is Apple's Restrictions payload key.

ALSO ON YOUR LEDGER, HONESTLY NOT DONE: MockSignalGridAPI's replayed-vectors question (design, waiting on your parity gate), the DemoMode flag table verification on the simulator, and the equalToConstant rows at accessibility-extra-large. The HostApp still has 5 fixed heights and 0 flexible - I reported that last session and did not fix it, and it is a real truncation risk now that the fonts scale.

ONE NON-REPO CAUSE WORTH RECORDING so you do not chase it: preflight's CycloneDX gate failed on this Mac over sonner@2.0.8, present in local node_modules but in NO manifest and not in pnpm-lock.yaml. The committed SBOM was correct; the install was stale. pnpm install --frozen-lockfile pruned it, lockfile and every manifest stayed byte-identical, gate passes. Nothing to fix on your side.
